name: Shawn Novak
status: Active. Player agent at VC Sports Group, reported to work from Hawaii. In November 2026 his client Teruaki Sato signed a 6-year contract with the Chicago Cubs, reported at $120 million. His client Tomoyuki Sugano is a free agent. He has given no interview that I could find.
summary: The American agent behind Teruaki Sato's move from Hanshin to the Cubs. He is not a famous name in the USA; his niche is Japan. He can interpret Japanese at a press conference, he negotiated a foreign pitcher's contract WITH Hanshin in 2019 before he ever negotiated against them, and Japanese papers describe him as the man who demanded, in writing, that Hanshin let Sato go.
quick_facts: Shawn Novak in English sources (MLB.com, MASN). Japanese papers write ショーン・ノバック, which is sometimes turned back into 'Sean'
Player agent, VC Sports Group (MLB.com called him 'VC Sports Group agent Shawn Novak' in Dec 2024)
Amuse Sports USA, in 2019 (one source: a reporter's post quoted by a Venezuelan sports site)
Hawaii, according to Sponichi (Oct 2026) and business directories. The agency itself is listed in Chicago
He interpreted for Tomoyuki Sugano at the Orioles' online press conference in Dec 2024 (MLB.com), so he works in Japanese
Tomoyuki Sugano ✅, Teruaki Sato ✅, Robert Suarez 🟡, Shota Morishita 🟡 (agency confirmed by tabloid and blog; Novak himself not confirmed)
A weekly magazine says he holds a New York State lawyer's licence. Single source, gossip-grade: not confirmed

sections.title: In short
sections.intro: Most Japanese stars pick a big American agency with a famous name. Sato picked a four-person firm and an agent almost unknown to US media. What that agent had was Japan: the language, a Hawaii base between the two countries, and a history with Hanshin from the other side of the table. The confirmed record is short, so this page separates three things: what solid sources say, what tabloids and magazines claim, and what I could not open.

cells: Late 2019
Pitcher Robert Suarez, then with SoftBank, agrees a 2-year, $6.75 million contract with Hanshin. A reporter's post says the deal was negotiated by Shaun Inouye and Shawn Novak of Amuse Sports USA.
🟡 single source (the page is dated about six years before Nov 2026; exact date not checked)
Oct–Nov 2024
Tomoyuki Sugano, 35, declares for MLB as a free agent and signs with VC Sports Group, 'the same agency as Mookie Betts'.
✅ agency confirmed (Tokyo Sports)
Dec 2024
Sugano signs with the Baltimore Orioles for 1 year, $13 million. Novak interprets for him at the press conference and relays his statement to local media.
✅ MLB.com and MASN name Novak
2024 offseason
Teruaki Sato signs with VC Sports Group as he first asks Hanshin about MLB.
🟡 reported (Sports Hochi)
Oct 2025 – Jan 2026
Contract talks between Sato and Hanshin run about three months. A Sankei columnist writes that Novak demanded a move after the 2026 season and wanted the posting promise put in writing.
🟡 a named column in a major paper, but the club and player denied a dispute
Sato signs for one year, the last player in Japan to do so. He says his agent and the club spent a long time on posting and salary.
✅ Sato's own words
Sugano pitches for the Colorado Rockies (12 wins, 12 losses, ERA 5.37) on a one-year deal listed by Spotrac at $5.1 million.
✅ agency; Novak's part not stated
Oct 2026

Hanshin approve Sato's posting. Sponichi names Novak as Sato's agent, 'the same as Sugano', and reports MLB scouts asking who will fly to Hawaii, his base. A blog citing Daily Sports and the tabloid Nikkan Gendai say teammate Shota Morishita has signed with the same agency.
✅ Sponichi for Novak and Sato; 🟡 Morishita
Sato agrees with the Cubs 23 days after talks open: 6 years, reported $120 million, above the $80 million forecast.
✅ deal; money is REPORTED

sections.title: Japanese and Japan-linked players
sections.intro: ✅ confirmed, 🟡 single source or reported, ⚪ unverified. 'Agency' means VC Sports Group; a player with the agency is not automatically Novak's own client.

cells: Tomoyuki Sugano
Yomiuri Giants ace; MLB from 2025 (Orioles, then Rockies)

MLB.com and MASN call Novak his agent in Dec 2024; he interpreted for him. Sponichi calls Novak his agent in Oct 2026. In Nov 2026 the Rockies said they were in contact with his agent about a new contract.
Teruaki Sato
Hanshin Tigers → Chicago Cubs, 2026
Sponichi (Oct 2026), the Sankei column and Nikkan Gendai all name Novak. US reports name only the agency.
Robert Suarez
Venezuelan pitcher; SoftBank, then Hanshin's closer 2020–2021; MLB since 2022

2019 Hanshin contract reported as negotiated by Novak and Shaun Inouye at Amuse Sports USA. A weekly magazine and an agent directory list him as a client now. Who negotiated his later MLB contracts was not checked.
Shota Morishita
Hanshin outfielder, still in Japan

Nikkan Gendai headline: 'same agent as Teruaki Sato'. A blog citing Daily Sports says he signed in 2026. The Sankei column mentions 'information' that Novak signed a young Hanshin player, without naming him.

sections.title: Method: how he seems to work
sections.intro: Built from the cases above. The first three points are sourced; the rest is my analysis.

rows: He speaks for the player in Japanese and English himself. At Sugano's Orioles introduction he was the interpreter, which a big agency would normally hire someone for.
https://www.mlb.com/news/tomoyuki-sugano-visits-baltimore-after-signing-with-orioles
He negotiates with the Japanese club, not only the American one. Sato said his agent and Hanshin talked through posting and salary together.
https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/6f3424a228fe40ccc674bc5bdff5766a875c13ba
He sits between the two countries. Sponichi reported MLB scouts discussing trips to Hawaii to meet him.
https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/8e92522c6c64927eebf2ce99c7cbd1f0f2c0d5c5

My analysis: he knew Hanshin's front office from the Suarez deal in 2019, when he was selling them a player. Six years later he was taking one away. That inside knowledge is probably his real edge, though no source says this is how Sato found him.
My analysis: he uses the yearly contract as leverage. Sato stayed unsigned until the day before camp and then signed for one year only, which kept the question open for October.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/01/31/0019970204.shtml
My analysis: he is building a line of Hanshin clients. If Morishita is his too, the club will meet the same agent again in a few years.
Not reported. In MLB the player normally pays the agent a percentage of the contract. No source gives his rate for Sato or Sugano.
Scale, for a sense of the stakes: if an agent's cut were a few percent of $120 million, it would be several million dollars. This is arithmetic on an unknown rate, not a reported figure.

sections.title: Rumours and unofficial reports (NOT facts)
sections.intro: You asked for these too. Everything in this table comes from tabloids, weekly magazines, anonymous insiders or columns. Each row says who claims it and what speaks against it. Do not treat any of it as established.

cells: He demanded that Hanshin put in writing that Sato could be posted after the 2026 season, a 'hard-line stance'.
Sankei column 'Onifude no Tora Manyuki' (Jan 2026); also 'it is said' by a sportswriter in Naigai Times.
Plausible and from a named columnist, but second-hand. Sato said it was not a fight. No written promise was reported; the club approved in October after the Triple Crown.

His forceful negotiating 'stirred up' the club, and the 500 million yen contract hid a problem: the club saw 200 million of it as a one-off reward for his titles, so the starting point for the next talks was left unclear.
Weekly Jitsuwa (Feb 2026), a gossip-leaning weekly.
Unconfirmed. Overtaken by events: there were no next talks with Hanshin.
His tactics 'completely backfired' and a move after 2026 was '100% gone', according to a former Hanshin player.
A magazine article carried by au Web Portal (1 Apr 2026); the speaker is not named.
Wrong as a prediction: Hanshin approved the posting six months later.
He holds a New York State lawyer's licence.
Weekly Jitsuwa.
Single source. Could be checked in the public New York attorney directory; I have not done so.
Sato might 'force through' a move and would not back down.
Nikkan Gendai (Aug 2026), quoting an anonymous management-industry insider.
The same insider guessed he might wait another year. He did not.
Morishita having 'the same agent' will make things harder for Hanshin.
Nikkan Gendai (Oct 2026).
Opinion. The club's stated rule is that a player's wish alone is never enough.
Sato's training with Mookie Betts (also a VC Sports Group client) was the Dodgers 'fencing him in'.
Tabloid pieces, Dec 2025.
He signed with the Cubs.
A Sankei columnist proposed a 'Tiger rule' on MLB moves so that agents cannot pull players out one after another.
Same Sankei column.
This is the columnist's proposal, not club policy. It shows how the Kansai press saw him: as a threat to the club's control.

sections.title: Controversies and criticism
sections.intro: No misconduct, sanction or legal problem was found (searched 27 Nov 2026, Japanese and English; a light check). The criticism is about style.

rows: Criticism: Kansai columnists and weeklies painted him as hard-line and as stirring up the club (see the rumour table).
https://topics.smt.docomo.ne.jp/article/sankei/sports/sankei-_sports_baseball_LZR37SCNSVLTFD354IXSOYWLVE

The defence: the result. His client got the posting within one season and a contract 50% above the market forecast, and thanked the club on the way out. Hanshin's head of baseball operations said the decision was the club's own overall judgement.
https://www.daily.co.jp/tigers/2026/10/19/0020945650.shtml
Note on sources: almost everything negative comes from anonymous voices in outlets that lean toward the club's side. He has not answered in public.
Read on 27 Nov 2026. Sato's deal is done. Sugano is unsigned, and the Rockies have added other starting pitchers, which Sports Hochi says may affect his return.
https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/55a226716f641a56d4759689d2e53a7f4459c4f4
Watch: whether Morishita asks Hanshin for posting, and whether Novak speaks at Sato's Chicago press conference on 30 Nov.
A small agent can beat big ones for a Japanese client if he covers the gap the big ones leave: the Japanese club, the language and daily contact.

The route in was a foreign player. Representing an import inside Japan (Suarez) gave him relationships with a Japanese front office, which later helped him sign Japanese stars. That is the reverse of the usual path.
The Japanese press treats an agent who talks to the club as a troublemaker. That says as much about how new this is in Japan as it does about him.
